locked_policy.rule: source_attribution does not imply detection. Assign detection only when the paper explicitly performs an authenticity / real-versus-generated task. Classification among already-synthetic generators is attribution only.
locked_policy.application: A real class inside an attribution protocol or rejection of an unknown synthetic generator alone does not establish substantively evaluated authenticity detection.

documents.title: Open Set Synthetic Image Source Attribution

identity.publication_relationship: Local curated publication review links this same title, three authors, arXiv ID, and method to BMVC 2023 paper 659. The author-deposited v1 and inaccessible BMVC final PDF were not compared for textual equivalence.

documents.title: ManiFPT: Defining and Analyzing Fingerprints of Generative Models

identity.publication_relationship: arXiv record states Accepted to CVPR 2024; canonical record identifies CVPR 2024 and DOI 10.1109/cvpr52733.2024.01026. Exact textual equivalence to the inaccessible CVF final PDF was not established.

actions.original_question: Does the BMVC protocol include a separate authenticity evaluation beyond unknown-generator rejection?
actions.claimed_forensic_task: Open-set synthetic image source attribution among known and unseen generator architectures.
actions.actual_output_and_decision_space: Nearest known-generator reference produces a candidate generator; normalized embedding distance accepts that generator or rejects the image as from an unseen synthetic generator (section 3, equations 5 and 8).
actions.authentic_image_role: Real datasets are listed as training data for image generators and camera-model identification is used only to initialize the embedding network. Section 4.1 source-attribution train/test data consist of seven synthetic generators; there is no authentic-image output class in the evaluated source protocol.
actions.authenticity_evaluation: No explicit real-versus-generated evaluation or authenticity metric in sections 4.1-4.5. Unknown means StyleGAN or Stable Diffusion images held out as synthetic-generator architectures, not authentic images.
actions.source_attribution_evaluation: Section 4.3 defines average F1 over five seen generator architectures and correct reject rate (CRR) for two unseen synthetic generators. Table 2 AUC of the average-F1-versus-CRR curve is 0.868 for pretrained MISLNet or Xception. Table 3 reports proposed method average F1 0.900 on seen generators and CRR 0.645 on unseen generators.
actions.confidence: high for the v1 protocol; BMVC-final equivalence unverified
actions.version_limitation: Author-deposited arXiv v1 is identity-matched to the locally linked BMVC work, but the inaccessible BMVC final PDF was not compared.
actions.reason: The evaluated decision is known-versus-unseen synthetic generator identity. Camera pretraining and generator-training real datasets do not make authenticity an output or scored task; T1 therefore does not support the current detection label in this manuscript.

actions.original_question: Does the full protocol evaluate real/fake detection in addition to fingerprint or model identification?
actions.claimed_forensic_task: Define model artifacts/fingerprints and use them for multiclass generative-model attribution; earlier binary detection work is motivation and comparison.
actions.actual_output_and_decision_space: A ResNet50-based model attributor outputs a source class under multiclass cross-entropy. Section 4.2 labels images 0=Real and 1..M=generative model identities; the Real class exists within the source classifier.
actions.authentic_image_role: Real datasets estimate the natural-image manifold and supply the Real source class in four attribution datasets. This is an integrated real class, not a separately reported binary authenticity experiment.
actions.authenticity_evaluation: No explicit binary real-versus-generated protocol, real-class accuracy, authenticity recall, AUC, or real-versus-synthetic confusion result is reported. Table 2 reports only overall multiclass source-attribution accuracy and feature separability; Table 4 reports cross-dataset attribution accuracy. The manuscript contrasts binary real/synthetic detection in earlier work with its multiclass model-attribution contribution.
actions.source_attribution_evaluation: Section 4.2 Table 2 reports overall attribution accuracy and Fréchet Distance Ratio on GM-CIFAR10, GM-CelebA, GM-CHQ, and GM-FFHQ. Best reported ManiFPT GM-CelebA accuracy is 74.7% for the SSL variant, and GM-CIFAR10 accuracy is 72.018% for the SL variant; neither is a binary detection score. Section 4.4 Table 4 scores cross-dataset attribution, and sections 4.5/appendix D score model-fingerprint clustering.
actions.confidence: moderate-high for the v2 evaluated tasks; a Real class is present but no authenticity-specific evaluation is reported, and CVF-final equivalence is unverified
actions.version_limitation: Author-deposited arXiv v2 is linked to CVPR 2024 by the record, but the inaccessible CVF final PDF was not compared.
actions.reason: The Real class makes authenticity predictions possible within a multiclass classifier, but T1 requires an explicitly performed and substantively evaluated authenticity task. The manuscript evaluates aggregate model-attribution accuracy and fingerprint structure, without a detection-specific result; retaining detection on class inclusion alone would overstate the evidence.
